claims.claim: Standard-code logical feasibility has an explicit linear-size 2-CNF encoding.
claims.strongest_challenge: Generic 2-SAT feasibility is prior work; Boolean bit moves are not automatically nucleotide substitutions.
claims.limitation: The result concerns declared logical constraints, not realizability or energetic stability of an RNA ensemble.
claims.decision: Retain the explicit code-specific representation and withhold a new generic 2-SAT claim.

claims.claim: Single-frame component signatures are complete and connected endpoint distance is nucleotide Hamming distance.
claims.strongest_challenge: Generic binary-CSP geodesicity is known, while partial Leu/Arg gates and two-bit nucleotide changes require the code-specific lifting argument.
claims.limitation: Extra motif, score or overlapping-frame constraints can invalidate the original signature. Finite checks corroborate the proof.
claims.decision: Retain with the single-frame and logical-obligation assumptions explicit.

claims.claim: Overlapping standard-code obligations admit an exact quotient with Cartesian fibres and nucleotide geodesics.
claims.strongest_challenge: Coarse orientation and serine signatures alone are insufficient; larger coordinate domains and complemented gates must preserve the quotient predicates.
claims.limitation: Arbitrary ordered logical triplets are more general than physical reading frames. The single-frame height-three bound does not extend to arbitrary overlaps.
claims.decision: Retain the stronger signature and distinguish compact witness cost from full sequence materialization.

claims.claim: Uniform completion counts have a conditional leucine factor two; route counting can be hard despite simple reachability.
claims.strongest_challenge: Independent-set inference, order polytopes and restricted linear-extension hardness are established. Reduction conventions cannot be strengthened silently.
claims.limitation: Leucine factor two is conditional and need not survive arbitrary codon weights. #P-completeness uses polynomial-time Turing reductions and an input-dependent number of logical targets, not exactly two physical structures.
claims.decision: Retain the precise specialization, separate arithmetic from bit cost, and do not assert broader physical-structure hardness.

claims.claim: Declared register geometries have phase-specific product classes and certified conditional scarcity rates.
claims.strongest_challenge: Fibonacci counts and transfer matrices are known; the increment is the code-specific register language and rates.
claims.limitation: No qualifying observed native coding register switch was recovered. Conditional uniform-peptide scarcity is not a universal native-gene or energetic law.
claims.decision: Retain as restricted-model mathematics, not an explanation of an observed biological switch.

claims.claim: The additive independent-set criterion identifies exactly when all nonempty superlevel graphs are connected.
claims.strongest_challenge: Independent-set geometry and additive decomposition are established; accurately predicting the coefficients is a separate problem.
claims.limitation: The theorem does not establish folding-specific interactions, occupancy change or functional rescue.
claims.decision: Retain as a conditional geometric criterion and do not infer score predictability from it.

claims.claim: Exact barrier ranges on rational affine polytopes are computable at fixed latent dimension; route quantifiers coincide universally exactly for a unique minimal connecting vertex set.
claims.strongest_challenge: Lattice-polynomial and arrangement machinery are established. Generic box corners fail, and a unique minimal connecting vertex set is not a unique simple path.
claims.limitation: Fixed dimension has a dimension-dependent exponent. Deterministic uncertainty sets are not calibrated confidence regions. Priority for specific reductions remains unverified.
claims.decision: Retain the explicit specialized statements, independent verification and limitations; withhold first-algorithm and biological calibration claims.

claims.claim: Factor-level additive-product closure supports exact endpoint connectivity, capacity and constructive witnesses.
claims.strongest_challenge: Additive merge-tree composition is established, and the closest detailed thesis construction was not fully accessible.
claims.limitation: No first or fastest algorithm claim. A component is not the retained part of its projection product. Witnesses need not be shortest; exact capacity is polynomial in bit complexity, not asserted strongly polynomial.
claims.decision: Retain the explicit query and verified bounds while marking algorithmic priority unresolved.

claims.claim: Generic score organization accounts for most of the original permutation contrast; the residual is not a demonstrated folding mechanism.
claims.strongest_challenge: Imperfect roughness matching, influential transcripts, model/context choice, ties and saturated fits can affect residual interpretation.
claims.limitation: Retrospective influence, tighter matching, unsaturated fits and tie checks retain the descriptive pattern but do not identify a mechanism. Additive fits are in sample; cluster intervals describe this modeled transcript collection, not biological-replicate uncertainty.
claims.decision: Withdraw an established RNA-specific preservation or evolutionary-advantage claim; retain the control result and bounded residual.

claims.status: Failed frozen computational pilot; design uninformative for mechanism
claims.claim: The original three-state barrier/intervention pilot did not pass its expansion criteria.
claims.strongest_challenge: Every three-state additive fit is saturated, so the design cannot distinguish additive from interacting fields.
claims.limitation: This is synthetic folding-model evidence, not biological rescue or disruption. Unsupported intervention directions cannot be omitted.
claims.decision: Preserve the failure and do not expand this motif into a folding-specific engineering result.

claims.status: Failed frozen efficiency criterion; certificate checks passed
claims.claim: Path/cut acquisition did not outperform the strongest included baseline.
claims.strongest_challenge: Established forward querying is the strongest included comparator; lower observed maxima do not establish a better arbitrary-input worst case.
claims.limitation: The interval covers Monte Carlo variation across 50 fixed-design seed blocks only. Forced-present endpoints are occupancy edits, not necessarily exact additive superlevel fields.
claims.decision: Retain the audited certificate workflow and negative comparison; retire held-out seeds from tuning.

claims.claim: The pairwise Gill predictor does not improve held-out RNA-library reproduction.
claims.strongest_challenge: The constant baseline outperforms the target; shared-reference shifts affect error, and the same genotypes occur in training and validation.
claims.limitation: This is held-out RNA-library reproduction conditional on previously inspected DNA, not independent genotype, protein-context or biological validation.
claims.decision: Keep the frozen failure without retuning or favorable-subset selection.

claims.claim: Gill positive observed-field barriers do not establish biological nonadditivity or a folding mechanism.
claims.strongest_challenge: Noise, reference anchoring and denominator changes can create apparent interactions and barriers; the nine fields reuse libraries.
claims.limitation: Library identities are mapped, but independent biological preparations, RNA/DNA pairing and simultaneous error calibration remain unresolved. A range of fieldwise maxima is not a fixed-pair barrier interval or a confidence region.
claims.decision: Report the measured contrasts and explicit dependence only; do not apply calibrated joint-uncertainty guarantees.

claims.claim: The GFP/URA3 programme has sequence-verified candidate groups but no completed defensible interaction prediction result.
claims.strongest_challenge: Shared mutants, normalized wild type and reporter dependence prevent treating candidate squares as independent observations; filtering and zero/subcutoff semantics remain inconsistent.
claims.limitation: Complete-double replicate covariance and exact source-processing provenance are missing. The eligibility stop is not a rejected biological hypothesis or a predictive benchmark failure.
claims.decision: Resolve measurement and processing semantics before further inference; retain the stopped executions.

claims.claim: The frozen mitochondrial structure-to-function test could not meet its transcript coverage gate.
claims.strongest_challenge: At most eleven transcript/bicistronic units are independent; cross-study structural and functional measurements lack established same-aliquot and exact condition matching.
claims.limitation: Local probing-mixture variance is not thermodynamic occupancy. Coverage failure does not refute ensemble effects on translation.
claims.decision: Preserve the closed outcome gate; recover adequate structural information before a newly recorded design.

claims.claim: The folding-derived connectivity hypothesis lacks a completed independent biological validation cohort.
claims.strongest_challenge: Reusing inspected sources, overlapping windows or related sequence material as validation would exaggerate independence.
claims.limitation: A specific missing authenticated structure/probing archive is a source gap, not proof that suitable data do not exist. RNA abundance is not direct structural occupancy or organismal function.
claims.decision: Bound the biology claims and identify each incomplete branch rather than presenting it as a negative experiment.

claims.claim: Projection and path certificates bound interacting product barriers, with exact improvement and failure examples and a sparse hardness boundary.
claims.strongest_challenge: Projection bounds and bucket elimination are known; singleton envelopes can miss interactions entirely.
claims.limitation: Actual elimination-order width, explicit envelope storage and witness output costs remain. No general sparse polynomial algorithm or approximation-hardness claim.
claims.decision: Retain the specialized certificate, counterexamples and exact reduction; no generic novelty claim.

claims.claim: Normalized Gill interaction residuals reproduce weakly across the fixed library comparison.
claims.strongest_challenge: High marginal count-field agreement does not imply normalized residual agreement; a simple cancellation construction demonstrates the logical gap.
claims.limitation: One related reporter system, shared libraries, unresolved biological preparations, historical coverage selection and nonlinear response alternatives.
claims.decision: Preserve failure and all controls. No biological noise ceiling, causal interaction or independent-gene validation claim.

claims.claim: One modeled ensemble feature does not meet its incremental prediction target in the selected PERSIST cohort.
claims.strongest_challenge: Strong sequence baselines and family-aware splitting remove an apparent advantage from merely adding a folding feature.
claims.limitation: One selected reporter context within one study; processing selection, unresolved preparation identity and physical endpoint calibration. MUP is calculated and constructs do not form complete paths.
claims.decision: Retain failure, no retuning or favorable subset. Do not generalize to all folding features or claim biological rescue.

claims.claim: Observation prices and optional batches can change exact optimal query cost on the declared six-bit model.
claims.strongest_challenge: Finite Bellman recursion and stochastic Boolean function evaluation are established methods. New cost tables do not repair the earlier failed acquisition comparison.
claims.limitation: Fixed graph, abstract costs and full-support product priors in the experiment. Generic correlated-prior extension needs positive-mass histories and logically universal certificates.
claims.decision: Retain as bounded exact comparison, not a new general algorithm or measured assay efficiency.

claims.status: Closed or gated source branches; not negative biological findings
claims.claim: PAXT, additional splicing and other proposed sources do not presently support the intended validated endpoint comparison.
claims.strongest_challenge: Public data availability alone does not establish that measurements answer the proposed synonymous-accessibility question.
claims.limitation: Missing metadata or incompatible endpoints could be resolved by future data recovery; no result is inferred from the missing analysis.
claims.decision: Stop expansion on these sources. Preserve the gap and required next evidence.

adaptation_boundary: No examined validation cohort is available for further tuning described as confirmation.
scope: Abstract mathematics, synthetic benchmarks and retrospective eligible reporter data. No new experimental engineering.
next_scientific_step: Recover biologically independent preparation and paired normalization metadata, or obtain an eligible independent complete genotype landscape. Do not increase model complexity on these failed validation sets.
